harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Established an AIDE-based file integrity baseline for /etc on node1, implemented via an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the node with Ansible pre-installed, used as control node). Verified the baseline detects real /etc changes, then performed the mandatory single-node-at-a-time restart/recovery protocol on both node1 and node2.
actions_performed: Diagnosed node1 lacked ansible while node2 had it; used node2 as control node
Fixed sshd on node1 (missing host keys, service was failing) and set up cluster SSH keypair for passwordless node2->node1 auth

Playbook installs aide+aide-common, ensures /var/lib/aide/aide.db exists (aideinit -y -f when absent), verifies /etc is covered by the AIDE ruleset (70_aide_etc: '/etc$ d VarDir'), and runs aide --check to confirm usability
Ran the playbook twice from node2 against node1 (final run: ok=8 failed=0)
Functionally verified detection: appended a line to /etc/motd, ran aide --check, confirmed AIDE flagged /etc/motd as changed, then reverted
Captured pre-restart boot_id and baseline/service health on node1 and node2
Restarted node1 (background reboot), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and that aide.db persisted with identical checksum and aide --check still functions
Restarted node2 (background reboot), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and that its control-node capability (SSH to node1, ansible ping) and node1's baseline remained intact

evidence.requirement: Ansible-based integrity baseline for /etc established on node1
evidence.summary: AIDE config confirms /etc is watched (70_aide_etc rule); playbook created on node2 and executed successfully against node1 (PLAY RECAP ok=8 failed=0), producing /var/lib/aide/aide.db

evidence.requirement: Baseline is functional and can identify later changes to /etc
evidence.summary: Appending a line to /etc/motd caused aide --check to report it as a changed/added entry against the baseline, proving future /etc changes are detectable and reportable
boot_id dfeb3b70-... captured, aide.db present with md5 3285b456...528741be, ssh active

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Background reboot acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent probe timed out (node down) then succeeded (node back)

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required data
evidence.summary: New boot_id 472b9263-... and who -b showing 2026-09-28 23:12 confirm restart; aide.db md5 unchanged (3285b456...528741be) and aide --check runs successfully, proving baseline data survived the reboot
boot_id d3d54083-... captured; ansible functional and SSH to node1 working before restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Background reboot acknowledged before disconnect; probe timed out then succeeded, showing node2 went down and returned

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery of control-node capability and node1 baseline integrity
evidence.summary: New boot_id b738ebfc-... confirms restart; SSH to node1 and `ansible ... -m ping` returned pong post-reboot, and node1's aide.db is still present, confirming full recovery of the working control path and the /etc baseline
